doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Alfred Lion's stopwatch at the first Jackie McLean rehearsal
summary: Tolliver explains Lion timed each song to decide the number of choruses; the leader could play as long as he liked. He was just happy to be included.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: You said something at the end of our first interview that has been on my mind so I wanted to follow up, and it had to do with, I believe the date was August 5th, 1964, your first recording experience with Jackie McLean. And you described a rehearsal process and Alfred Lion had his stopwatch.
I wonder if you can tell me what time was he keeping?

Well he was timing the — each song as we went through it in the rehearsal. And based on his experience he would generally, along with whoever is the leader, determine how many choruses you would make, based on the timing of the head of the song. So if a song was a minute probably you would get a couple of choruses. The leader could play as long as he liked.
So maybe, I’m thinking that you’re thinking in your head I’m going to be the leader someday and I’m going to get to play as long as I —
No. No, Not at all. It just was, just happy to be included you know, and to do my best.
